articles.body: It usually starts with a message at 11pm: "学长，帮我看看这个合同能签吗？" — "can you take a quick look at this contract before I sign it tomorrow?" Someone's first freelance gig, a studio hiring a friend as an editor, a startup sending an NDA before an interview. Nobody wants to pay a lawyer for a two-page NDA. Everybody signs anyway. I'm a law master's student in China. After the thirtieth "quick look", I noticed I was running the same checklist every single time: Is confidentiality perpetual? Does it auto-renew? Is liability uncapped? Does their IP assignment quietly swallow my friend's background work? Does it end with 最终解释权归甲方所有 — "final interpretation belongs to Party A"? So I automated myself.

articles.title: The dependency problem behind CVE-2026-103877: patching a library that hides inside other software
articles.excerpt: The dependency problem behind CVE-2026-103877: patching a library that hides inside other software Vulnerability overview CVE-2026-103877 is a deserialization flaw in the Apache Directory LDAP API, fi…
articles.body: The dependency problem behind CVE-2026-103877: patching a library that hides inside other software Vulnerability overview CVE-2026-103877 is a deserialization flaw in the Apache Directory LDAP API, fixed in releases 2.1.9 and 1.2.9 after the October 2, 2026 Apache advisory set. The classification is CWE-502. No exploitation in the wild and no public proof-of-concept have been reported. Mechanism and exploitation conditions The schema exchange is the attack point. A rogue server, or an attacker positioned before TLS is established, answers a schema request with a serialized Java class. When the client processes that object, the advisory states there is potential for remote code execution. The attacker needs no credentials, only control of the responding endpoint.

articles.title: RBAC Is Not Enough: Thinking About Authorization in Enterprise Systems
articles.excerpt: Roles are one of the first authorization mechanisms most backend developers encounter. For example: admin manager user The server checks the user's role and allows or rejects an operation. That is use…
articles.body: Roles are one of the first authorization mechanisms most backend developers encounter. For example: admin manager user The server checks the user's role and allows or rejects an operation. That is useful. But enterprise systems quickly demonstrate that roles alone are often insufficient. The NIS Store MIS example The system I have been working on above includes roles representing different responsibilities. These include: system administrator; operational administrator; store administrator; multi-layered approving authority store manager; store officer; department officer; request officer; dispatch officer; auditor. The important observation is that a person's role does not necessarily tell us everything about what they can access.

articles.body: What's up DEV Community👋 I’m Richard from MangoBoost, and we just launched Mango Inference, an API for serving open-weight models including DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, and MiniMax M3. It’s OpenAI-compatible, so switching usually means changing your base_url, API key, and model name, with no other code changes. A couple of things people usually ask about: Data retention: Zero data retention is on by default. We don’t store your prompts or outputs. The one exception is a short-lived prefix cache, which makes repeated prompts faster and cheaper and isn’t tied to your account. Agents and long sessions: that same cache stays alive [for about an hour], so resumed agent sessions can keep hitting it instead of paying full price to resend the whole context.

articles.body: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV. articles.body: SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. The company sent 27 of its Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) today (Oct. 12), launching them atop a Falcon 9 rocket from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:28 p.m. EDT (5:28 p.m. local time; 0028 GMT on Oct. 13) It was the first Starlink mission for a Falcon 9 since Sept. 19 , which was another 27-satellite liftoff from Vandenberg. For some perspective on this recent gap: Between Aug. 19 and Sept. 6, a span of 19 days, SpaceX launched seven Starlink missions with Falcon 9s. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a ship at sea shortly after the Oct. 12 launch. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX did loft a batch of Starlinks after that, but it wasn't aboard a Falcon 9.

articles.body: Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies. The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster . The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research
articles.excerpt: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency…
articles.body: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, advancing research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration. This research supports astronaut health during long-duration missions through four investigations from the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences division, including 3D models of the human brain, a crop disease study, a faster way to assess astronaut health, and an analysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria aboard the space station.
